Subject: Dedicated renewal & capacity scale: 16 → 32 GPUs — options and draft terms

Hi Julia,

Thanks again for the heads up about your upcoming renewal. Per our intake, your current Dedicated reserved pool (16 GPUs, 12mo term) is up for renewal mid-December. I wanted to put a clear set of options on the table for scaling to 32 GPUs and how pricing + SLOs would be handled so your procurement and infra teams can review.

High-level options (illustrative):
- Option A — Renew 16 GPUs for 12 months at current baseline rate (status quo).
- Option B — Upgrade to 32 GPUs, 12-month commit. Proposed reserved per-GPU rate: $3.50/hr (per reserved GPU hour). Throughput target: baseline throughput of ~1.1M tokens/min across the pool (aggregate), 99.9% availability SLA.
- Option C — Upgrade to 32 GPUs, 24-month commit. Discounted per-GPU reserved rate: $3.10/hr. Includes a 30% burst buffer for short spikes and optional quarterly re-eval.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short term-sheet (RWI-16to32-pricing-terms-v2.pdf) with line-item math and an amendment template you can share with procurement. Key notes: pricing above is per reserved GPU hour (not per-instance hour), networking egress remains billed per usage, and we offer a throughput guarantee with service credits tied to availability.

If you want, we can carve out a mutual action plan (one-pager) and route a redline for your legal/procurement teams — I can coordinate that with our AE and ops. What timeline do you have for finalizing?

Best,

Hiro Tanaka

Looping in Marcus (AE) and Dev (Legal/Deals) to provide the concrete numbers and the amendment sample.

Quick answers inline:
- Monthly cost math (illustrative):
  • Option B (32 GPUs @ $3.50/hr): 32 * $3.50 * 720 = $80,640/mo.
  • Option C (32 GPUs @ $3.10/hr): 32 * $3.10 * 720 = $71,424/mo.
  • Current 16 GPU run-rate (assume $3.80/hr last term): 16 * $3.80 * 720 = $43,776/mo.
  • Incremental cost from current -> Option B: +$36,864/mo.

- SLA / credits: our standard availability SLA for Dedicated is 99.9% over monthly window. For this amendment we can formalize a throughput SLO (aggregate tokens/sec floor) with a credit schedule: 5% credit for monthly availability between 99.5–99.9%, 15% credit for <99.5%. Dev will attach the precise legal language and examples.

- Mid-term price cap: we can commit to no upward price adjustment on reserved per-GPU rate for the first 12 months of any new commit. For multi-year (24mo) deals we typically include a CPI cap (<=3%/yr) or a fixed 2% cap — Marcus and Dev, please propose phrasing.

Next steps: Marcus — can you attach the redline and a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) so Big Retail can run procurement? Dev — please add the amendment and credit calculation examples.

Thanks,
Hiro

Daniel / Julia — attaching the one-pager MAP and the redline amendment as requested. Summary of the final commercial proposal we discussed:

- Final offer (agreed-for-signature):
  • 32 GPUs reserved pool, 12-month commit.
  • Final reserved rate: $3.25/hr per GPU (applies to all reserved hours).
  • Throughput SLO: aggregate baseline 1.1M tokens/min sustained; 99.9% availability SLA.
  • Price protection: no upward adjustment to reserved per-GPU rate for the first 12 months. Thereafter a CPI-linked adjustment capped at 2%/yr.
  • Service credits: 5% credit between 99.5–99.9% availability; 15% credit if availability <99.5%.

- Cost example (Option B final): 32 * $3.25 * 720 = $74,880/mo. 
- 95th-percentile monthly spend estimate (including typical burst): $82k/mo (this assumes ~10% burst buffer usage).
